summary: The comments emphasize the importance of the E-Rate program for school districts, libraries, and students. They argue against eliminating or significantly restructuring the program, limiting consultant fee structures, and dictating how schools use technology to support learning. The comments highlight the financial burden, loss of flexibility, and loss of expertise that such changes would impose. They also stress the need for local educators to make decisions about technology use based on the ne The comment period is too short and the timing is unfair. The scope of this NPRM is unprecedented. It covers the future of the program itself, how consultants are regulated, how CIPA is interpreted, how consortium members file certifications, and whether the FCC should take a position on classroom technology use. These are not narrow technical questions. They require careful analysis, coordination among district staff and state agencies, and input from the communities most affected. I support th

claims.requested_action: allow schools to evaluate and select consulting support based on individual needs
claims.argument: A single federally mandated approach to consultant compensation does not recognize the differences among schools and libraries or the variety of ways applicants access the expertise necessary to successfully participate in E-Rate
claims.evidence_quote: The Commission should focus on transparency, accountability, and preventing misconduct rather than restricting the choices available to compliant schools and libraries
